8.1.intro: A clean Google setup means every dollar is tracked and nothing changes without you. Let's do it once.

steps.say: In Google Ads, open **Admin > Access and security**. Check that you are an admin owner.
steps.check: Your email has Admin access. An agency owns it? Ask them in writing to give it to you.
steps.lost: Check your email is listed as Admin.

steps.say: In Shopify, install the **Google & YouTube** app. Connect Google Ads and Merchant Center (where Google keeps your product list).
steps.check: Both are connected and products are syncing.

steps.say:
Make purchases the only thing that counts.

1. Click **Goals > Conversions > Summary**.
2. Make **Purchase** the only **Primary** action. Set others to **Secondary**.
3. Turn on **Enhanced conversions**.
steps.check: Only Purchase is Primary. Enhanced conversions say "Active".
steps.careful: Check monthly. Other actions sometimes sneak back to Primary.

steps.say: In the Shopify Google app, connect Google Analytics 4. Then in Google Ads, open **Admin > Linked accounts** and link GA4.
steps.check: GA4 shows purchases and is linked.

steps.say: In **Tools > Shared library > Audience manager**, make three audiences: site visitors, buyers, and your email list.
steps.check: Three audiences show.

steps.say: Open **Recommendations**. Click **Auto-apply**. Untick everything.
steps.check: Google can't change campaigns without your click.

steps.say: Rename each campaign with the pattern from Lesson 6.7. Click the name, then the pencil.
steps.check: Every name shows number, type and job.

8.2.intro: Shopping ads are built from your product list. Better product info means better, cheaper ads.

steps.say: Rewrite titles with search words first: brand, product type, key feature. Example: "Acme Linen Shirt, Men's, Relaxed Fit, Sand".
steps.check: Your top 20 products have search-first titles.
steps.lost: Rewrite your best seller's title first.

steps.say: Use a clean main photo: just the product, plain background.
steps.check: No text or logos on main photos.
steps.lost: Swap one busy main photo for a clean one.

steps.say: Check feed prices and shipping match your site. Add barcode numbers (GTINs) if you have them.
steps.check: Merchant Center shows no mismatches.
steps.lost: Check one product's price matches your site.

steps.say: Add your own labels, like margin level, best seller or season.
steps.check: Products can be grouped by label.

steps.say: In Merchant Center, open **Products > Diagnostics**. Fix every error.
steps.check: Zero errors.

8.3.intro: Start Google simple. Add more campaigns as you grow.

steps.say: Small store? Run two campaigns: brand search, plus one product campaign (a feed-only Performance Max, or Shopping).
steps.check: You have brand search and one product campaign.

steps.say: In Performance Max, give it only your product feed. Add your brand name under **Brand exclusions**.
steps.check: PMax spends on new searches. Brand search covers your name.

steps.say: As you grow, add search for your top search words, and split PMax by best sellers or margin.
steps.check: Bigger accounts get more control.

steps.say: Much bigger? Add new-customer campaigns, competitor search, Demand Gen, and one campaign per country.
steps.check: Each campaign has one job.
steps.careful: Standard Shopping gives more control over searches. Use it if PMax spends where you can't control.

8.4.intro: Keywords are the search words you want to show for. Buying words bring buyers.

steps.say: List buying words: "buy", "best", "price", or product type plus a feature, like "linen shirt men".
steps.check: You have 20 to 50 keywords.
steps.lost: Write ten search words a buyer would type.

steps.say: In **Tools > Keyword Planner**, check monthly searches and competition for each.
steps.check: Each keyword has a number and a level.
steps.lost: Check your top five in Keyword Planner.

steps.say: Group keywords by theme. Five or fewer per ad group.
steps.check: Each group is tightly themed.

steps.say: Make a shared negative list (words you never want, like "free" or "jobs") in **Shared library > Negative keyword lists**. Apply it to every campaign.
steps.check: Wasted searches are blocked everywhere.

8.5.intro: Search ads are short. Every line has to earn its spot.

steps.say: Write up to 15 headlines: product plus benefit, the offer, proof, urgency, your brand. Pin 1 or 2 so they always show.
steps.check: Ad strength says "Good" or "Excellent".

steps.say: Write descriptions with reasons to buy, shipping and returns, and what to do next.
steps.check: Each answers "why here, why now".

steps.say: Add extras: sitelinks to best collections, callouts like "Free shipping", lists of styles, and images.
steps.check: Your ad takes more space.

8.6.intro: Target ROAS tells Google how much in sales you want for each $1 of ads. Base it on your break-even.

steps.say: Work out break-even ROAS: 1 ÷ (1 − VCR). With VCR at 45%, that's about 1.82.
steps.check: You have your break-even ROAS.

steps.say: In the campaign's **Bidding**, set target ROAS above break-even with room for profit. Example: 2.4 if break-even is 1.82.
steps.check: Google aims for a target that leaves profit.
steps.lost: Set it a bit above break-even.

steps.say: Change targets by about 10% at a time.
steps.check: Bidding stays steady.

8.7.intro: New customers grow the store. Google can favour them.

steps.say: Upload your customer list in **Audience manager > Your data segments**.
steps.check: Google knows who already bought.

steps.say: In the campaign's **Customer acquisition** setting, choose "Bid higher for new customers" or "Only bid for new customers".
steps.check: The campaign favours new buyers.
steps.careful: Only accept lower ROAS for new customers if they come back and buy again.

8.8.intro: Ten to twenty minutes once a week keeps Google profitable. Most waste hides in search terms.

steps.say: Open **Insights and reports > Search terms**. Tick searches that cost money but never sell, click **Add as negative keyword**. Tick searches that sell, click **Add as keyword**.
steps.check: Waste is blocked, winners are targeted.

steps.say: Check **Performance Max insights** for top products, searches and assets.
steps.check: You know your top PMax products.
steps.lost: Look at your top PMax product.

steps.say: Find campaigns marked "Limited by budget". If they hit your target, raise the budget about 20%.
steps.check: Good campaigns aren't held back.

steps.say: Compare brand and non-brand spend. Fix new errors in **Merchant Center > Diagnostics**.
steps.check: You know your non-brand spend, and the feed is clean.

8.9.intro: Demand Gen shows short videos and pictures on YouTube, Discover and Gmail. Your best social videos often work there.

steps.say: Export your 3 best social videos in vertical and horizontal.
steps.check: You have video files ready.
steps.lost: Pick your best video. Export two shapes.

steps.say: Make a Demand Gen campaign with those videos, aimed at buyers, visitors and lookalikes.
steps.check: The campaign is live.

steps.say: Judge it by people who saw it and bought later, and by your total MER.
steps.check: You judge the whole-store effect.
steps.lost: Look at total MER, not just clicks.

8.10.intro: Big sales change shoppers overnight. Google needs a nudge to keep up.

steps.say:
Tell Google a sale is coming.

1. Click **Tools > Budgets and bidding > Seasonality adjustments**.
2. Add one for the first 1 to 2 days of the sale.
3. Set the expected change to what you saw in past sales.
4. Set the end date.
steps.check: It's scheduled for the sale dates.
steps.lost: Add a seasonality adjustment for sale day one.

steps.say: Add promotions and sale prices to your product feed.
steps.check: Shopping ads show the sale price.
steps.lost: Add sale prices to the feed.

steps.say: Raise budgets slowly in the week before.
steps.check: Campaigns have enough money at the start.
steps.lost: Raise budgets a little each day before.

8.11.intro: Google keeps adding AI features automatically. They can help, if you check them.

steps.say: Open **Campaigns**. Look at any campaign Google upgraded automatically.
steps.check: You know which use AI features.

steps.say: Read the AI-written ad text. Check every page it sends people to.
steps.check: Ads say only what you're happy with.
steps.lost: Read one AI ad. Fix anything wrong.

steps.say: Check brand exclusions are still on. Check search terms and negatives twice a week.
steps.check: AI doesn't spend on your brand or junk.
steps.lost: Check brand exclusions are still there.

8.12.intro: Google tries to rush you into a "smart" campaign. We'll skip that and build two simple ones: brand search and Performance Max. Helix doesn't connect to Google Ads yet, so you'll click along.

steps.say: Go to ads.google.com, click **Start now**. When it asks for a campaign, find the small link **Switch to Expert Mode** or **Create an account without a campaign**. Click it.
steps.check: You're making an account, not a campaign.
steps.lost: Look for the small link at the bottom.

steps.say: Pick your country, time zone and currency carefully. Untick the strategist calls and promo emails. Click **Submit**.
steps.check: The account is made.
steps.careful: Time zone and currency can't change later. Double-check.
steps.lost: Check time zone and currency. Then submit.

steps.say: Add a payment method under **Billing**.
steps.check: A card or bank account is saved.

steps.say: In Shopify, install **Google & YouTube**. Click **Get started**. Connect your Google account, Merchant Center and Google Ads. Skip any campaign it offers.
steps.check: Green ticks for accounts, products syncing and conversion settings.
steps.lost: Install the app. Connect everything. Skip campaigns.

steps.say: In Google Ads: **Goals > Conversions > Summary**. **Edit goal** on Purchases, check it's **Primary**. Set page view and add to cart to **Secondary**. Save.
steps.check: Only Purchase counts.

steps.say: Click **+ Create > Campaign**. Choose **Sales** with **Purchase**, then **Search**. Name it "01-Search-Brand".
steps.check: A Search campaign is open.

steps.say: Under **Bidding**, choose **Target impression share**. Set **Anywhere on results page** to 90%. Set **Maximum CPC bid limit** to $0.50 to $1.
steps.check: Your ad shows for your name at a capped cost.

steps.say: Under **Networks**, untick **Search partners** and **Display Network**. Add countries you ship to. In **Location options**, pick **Presence**.
steps.check: It runs only on Google search, where you ship.
steps.lost: Untick both networks. Add your countries.

steps.say: Add your brand as keywords both ways: `[your brand]` and `"your brand"`, plus misspellings. Write one ad with 10 to 15 headlines and 4 descriptions. Budget $5 to $10 a day. Click **Publish campaign**.
steps.check: Status is "Eligible" (maybe "Under review" for a few hours).
steps.lost: Brand keywords, one ad, $5 a day, publish.

steps.say: Click **+ Create > Campaign**. Choose **Sales**, then **Performance Max**. Pick your product feed. Under **Bidding**, choose **Conversion value** with no target yet. Set a daily budget inside your guide (Lesson 1.9).
steps.check: PMax is connected to your products with a budget.
steps.lost: **Create**, **Performance Max**, pick your feed, set budget.

steps.say: In the asset group, remove extra headlines, images, videos and sitelinks where Google allows (**Edit**, then **x**). Add your brand under **Brand exclusions**. Click **Publish campaign**.
steps.check: PMax runs mostly from your feed.

steps.say: Leave both for 7 days. Then compare spend, purchases and ROAS with your break-even ROAS.
steps.check: You know if each is above or below break-even.
steps.careful: Don't apply Google's recommendations without reading each one. Keep auto-apply off.
steps.lost: Wait 7 days. Compare ROAS with break-even.

8.13.intro: Google Ads hides a lot behind menus. You only need a few screens.

steps.say: Open ads.google.com. Check the account name and ID at the top.
steps.check: You're in the right account.

steps.say: Click **Campaigns**. Set the date to **Last 7 days**.
steps.check: You see last week.

steps.say: Click **Columns**. Add **Conv. value** and **Conv. value / cost**. Click **Apply**.
steps.check: You see sales and ROAS per campaign.

steps.say: Click **Insights and reports > Search terms**.
steps.check: You know where wasted searches are.
steps.careful: Google moves menus often. Use the search box at the top and type the page name.
